The dark is held · build, then let it go

A tower defense descent

The Last Lamp

Five floors down. One flame. Everything in the dark wants it out.

How the dark works

  • The lamp burns at the center of every floor. Creatures follow the path toward it, and each one that arrives drains its oil. When the oil runs out, the run is over.
  • You can only build inside light. Candle Wards carry light outward, and the lamp's Wick branch widens its own. The Lamplighter's Signal Candles are the exception: one can stand in the dark within 4 tiles of a lit one.
  • Light has to connect. A candle only shines if it stands in light that leads back to the lamp. Take away a candle in that chain and everything past it is lost. If the light shrinks on its own, anything cut off goes dark and does nothing until the light returns. A Signal Candle's light also leaps to another Signal Candle up to 4 tiles away; a dotted thread shows each leap, and cutting it cuts everything past it.
  • The dark hides them. Out of the light, creatures are only shapes and eyes, and your wards cannot hit them. Shades and Abyssal Stalkers stay hidden even in lamplight. Only candles, bound Watchers, Flare, flare bolts, kindled creatures and a few upgrades unveil them.
  • Upgrades branch. Tap a ward or the lamp to open its three branches. Each can take two of them, and only one can reach its capstone. Everything you build is stripped when the floor ends, and you get half of it back.
  • Hold the dark. The hourglass beside Call the dark stops everything on the stair, and you can still place, upgrade and dismantle while it is held. It is not a break between waves: nothing built in a wave comes back whole, rites wait, and souls cannot be bound until you let it go.
  • Targeting. Harpoons, Censers and single-target horrors can aim at the first creature in line, the last, or the strongest.
  • Free undo. Anything you place or upgrade between waves refunds in full if you dismantle it before calling the dark.
  • Waves are drawn. Each floor draws its waves from a deck, so no two descents meet the same dark. The strip above the board names the next wave and shows what it brings. Waves with a boss or the Choirmaster keep their place.
  • Call early. Once a wave has finished arriving, you can call the next one while stragglers still walk, for bonus essence.
  • Binding. Some creatures leave a violet sigil when they die. Tap it before it fades and that creature joins your roster. Bound horrors are placed like wards and hit far harder. Slay the Keeper Below and its soul lingers longer than most. Bind it and it fights for you on the last floor. The Galvanist binds nothing by ritual: he captures with his Grounding Anchor instead. A bound Shrieker screams Choirmasters and Heralds back only a third as far, and no scream moves the same one again for 3 seconds, however many Shriekers you field.
  • Forks. On some floors the stair splits. They take the darker way, and only light you cast counts, never the lamp's. A gold chevron at the fork shows where they will go. Shades and Stalkers do the opposite and hunt your light. Gnashers and bosses keep the main way. A Weir built on the fork shuts one way; flip it between waves. Watchers fly over it, and a Behemoth breaks it. On these floors you also hold the Will-o’-Wisp: tap a way at a fork and, for eight seconds, everything but a boss follows it there.
  • Heralds. Some floors send a Herald: a named terror in one wave, shown on the strip above the board in the break before it comes. It drains 8 oil if it reaches the lamp, but it is no boss and never ends the run by itself. Kill it and it pays a relic. Floors two to four each send one, and a descent never meets the same one twice. The Last Keeper carries a lamp of its own, and every candle it passes goes out for 6.5 seconds (a Tuning Fork falls silent). The Tithe-taker takes 2 essence a second while it walks in your light; kill it and the sack bursts, paying it all back and half again. In the break before a Herald's wave, a red ring marks the rift it will climb out of. The Bellfather strikes its great bell every 5 seconds, and wards within 2.2 tiles reel and do nothing for 2 seconds. No Herald can be held for long: after 3 seconds stunned or pinned it breaks free, and shrugs off every hold for 3 seconds. A boss's rift is marked the same way in the break before its wave, with a wider, doubled ring and two marks: it always climbs out there.
  • Heavy creatures. Trench Behemoths cannot be stunned or pushed back, and nothing slows them by more than 15%. Plan to out-damage them.
  • Madness. Every horror you field adds madness. At Whispers the lamp flickers. At Slipping a horror may break loose when a wave begins, and you may start to see eyes in the dark that are not there. When the dark leans in, the lamp shrinks and everything but a boss moves faster.
  • Dread. The Many-Mouthed adds dread, striped at the end of the madness bar, and so does every sleeper you wake on The Carry, for the floor below it. Dread counts with madness toward every tier, but only the madness of horrors you paid for makes the Occultist stronger or opens free horrors. Dread brings only the dark.
  • Wards. Your kit names the wards you start with: Candles, Harpoons, Salt, Hook Traps set on the path, the Tithe Bowl that pays for every death near it, the Hex Effigy that makes everything near it take more damage, and its own. The Bone Chime, Tar Censer, Galvanic Coil and Whaling Gun are found on the stair: as gifts, from merchants, or in a pack. Only the Bellringer starts with the Chime.
  • Chimes. A Bone Chime stuns everything in its ring, but the ring spreads thin: the four nearest take its full strike, the rest half. A boss it stuns goes deaf to every chime for 4 seconds, and a dull grey ring shows it shrugging them off.
  • Combinations. Lightning does double to anything standing in salt. Once a Chime reaches Deathknell, anything stunned, held or pinned takes 30% more. Traps catch Shades and Stalkers without light, and so do the Occultist's Grasping Dead. Effigies make every other ward hit harder, and Unmasking shows what the dark hides. The Whaling Gun does double damage to Behemoths, elites and bosses.
  • Kits. Every descent starts with a kit. Each kit builds its own version of some wards and casts its own rites: the Lamplighter's Signal Candles pass light across the dark, its Flare Harpoons light what they strike, Kindle sets a creature burning and running, lighting the dark around it, and its Signal Mirror, built in the lamp's own light, reflects it in a 5-tile beam you aim between waves (it locks while the dark comes); you can build in the beam, and it burns what crosses it. The Galvanist builds a power grid: Pylons string live wires that shock, stun and light what crosses them, if a pylon stands in the lamp's own light to power the rest; his Arc Lamps burn bright but flicker; his Lightning Rods plant where they strike and join the grid; Overload fires every wire at once for 2 oil, and run hot it fries his pylons; he binds nothing by ritual: his Grounding Anchor forces nearby pylons to link to it, and a bindable creature that dies inside one of its triangles is caught in a cage to tap (the Keeper's core waits 15 seconds for a cage, and its fall readies the Anchor), each capture drawing 2 Heat out of the grid; his lamp's Dynamo branch ends in a Static Burst. The Occultist's Corpse Candles are free and need no lamp, but stand only beside bones from this floor (a pile holds three, and the floor keeps the freshest twelve) and go out when the wave ends; a full pile of three can rise as the Grasping Dead, arms that hold each creature crossing them for 2 seconds, six times; its Bone Spears and its horrors hit harder with every tier of madness, Raise the Dead stands a pile of bones up as a Risen that bites until the wave breaks, and Unbind sends a horror charging down the stair for good. The Bellringer, Agathe Vell, sees by sound: her Toll rings the lamp, and whatever its ring touches is heard for 1.5 seconds, outlined in the dark, veiled or not, and every ward can strike it, until its echo fades to a ghost; each Toll makes 1 Noise (it fades 1 every 8 seconds), and at 5 the dark answers with two Abyssal Stalkers; the Great Bell is heard across the whole floor for 3 Noise; her Bell Wires can be strung anywhere on the path, even in the dark, and hear what crosses them; she builds no candles: her Tuning Forks give no light but hum, standing within 5 tiles of the lamp or 3.5 of another fork, and she can build inside a hum even in the dark, though wards there strike only what is heard; a toll that reaches a fork rings again from it; a toll from the lamp echoes back off the walls of the floor; heavy things leave red footsteps where they tread unseen, but Shades, Stalkers and fliers make none; her Clapper Harpoons ring what they strike and knock it back, and the path's edges show for her even where it is dark; her lamp's Peal branch makes it toll on its own, with no Noise, but that heartbeat finds only the ordinary dark; tap Toll on the beat (a ring closes on the lamp, and the button glows) for a Perfect Toll that reaches half again as far and rings out faster, though it makes as much Noise as any toll; her Tolls, Great Bell, Bell Wires, Clapper bolts and Tocsin shells crack what they strike, and three cracks shatter it, hurting and cracking what stands beside it (bosses take 8, Behemoths and elites 5); her Tocsin shells any Bell Wire that jangles, however far away. The Whaler's Blubber Lamps burn wider but drink the lamp's oil unless its Try-pot renders oil from the dead, and its Tether Harpoons hold what they hit on a line that slows it; Haul Away casts a whaling net that hauls everything under it, and everything on its lines, 3 tiles back and tangles it. Every Blubber Lamp drinks as a wave begins: a measure from a Try-pot, which renders the dead into whale oil, or 1 oil from the lamp. What is left in the pots when a floor ends pours into the lamp. You start with the Lamplighter; other kits are earned by deeds down the stair or in the Ember Hall. Wards outside your kit can be found as gifts, in merchants, or off the stair.
  • The Roster. Five went down the stair the night Saltmouth drowned: Ambrose Fenn the lamplighter, Jonah Tolland the harpooner, the Nameless, Dr. Lucan Voss and Agathe Vell. Each carries the lamp their own way. Some are earned by a deed on the stair, some in the Ember Hall. Every kind of horror you bind or capture, on any descent, adds its eyes to the Nameless’s hood, for good: there are six to find.
  • Saltmouth. Walk Saltmouth from the title to stand in the drowned port above the stair. Tap the ground to walk there, or hold and drag to steer. The Head-frame over the shaft in the square takes you down: it asks who carries the lamp, as Descend does. The town climbs the cliff in two shelves: the square, the lane and the shore below, and up either stair the Rise, with the cemetery, the Keeper's Lodge and the Cracked Belfry. Four overgrown plots, the north acre under the cemetery, the black wood on the Rise, the net-lofts and the drowned strand on the shore, stay shut until you open each one's gate once with the haul; inside, nothing clears itself: in Build, tap a piece of debris to see what clearing it costs or gives back, clear only what you like, and build only on ground you have cleared. Nothing grows back. At the shore a ruined dock runs out into the sea with a boat tied at its end; the haul restores it, and you can walk out to the boat. In Settings, Start in Saltmouth opens the game there instead of on the title. Every descent hauls up timber, iron, tallow and curios from cleared floors, slain Heralds and bosses, and the stair's toll renders tallow for the town. Build spends it about the town: cobbles, boardwalk, street-lamps, braziers, fences and trees. Tap a piece you built to lift it and set it down elsewhere; ⟳, or a tap on the lifted piece, turns it an eighth at a time (paths and fences a quarter), and holding turns it back; Store puts it away whole, to set down again for nothing, and Salvage in Storage gives back all it cost; Undo takes back your last ten deeds. Grid sets pieces on the tiles, Free wherever your thumb puts them. Nothing may wall off the Head-frame. Each lamp that goes out below leaves a name waiting, and a Mossy Headstone carves it: tap the stone to read where it went out, with its stair's code to copy. The Keepers you have freed stand about the town, in the square and on the Rise, each at their own footing; a dark footing is one you have not freed, and a tap on it says what frees them. Talk to a Keeper to carry the lamp down as them, or to set them to a chore: while you are down they put timber, iron, tallow or curios by for every floor you clear, and the haul brings it up. Never embers, nothing on the stair. Nothing built may stand on a Keeper's place or wall one in. The tray's first chip turns to the next group of pieces (paths, lights, benches, plants, stones, fences and the Keepers' huts): a path you lay meets the earth with a rim of its own; a variant with a padlock waits for a pack from the Peddler; a Keeper's hut opens once they are freed, one each, and they stand at its door (a tile kept clear like their footing) when they are not at work. Paint repaints a building that stands in one of three muted colourways for 4 tallow, paid back when it goes to its own colours. Five ruined workshops stand about the town — the Ember Brazier and the Galvanic Smithy on the lane west of the square, the Ossuary Menagerie east of it, the Try-Works on the shore and the Cracked Belfry on the Rise — and the haul restores them, then lights their windows. Each restored workshop offers a town gift at its door: you may carry one town gift down per descent, and each one exacts a price on the stair; it is off on a replayed stair and on any floor under a Trial. Some landings after floors 2, 3 and 4 hang a cage behind one door, at most once a descent: pay the lock and whoever is in it climbs to Saltmouth with your haul, even if your lamp goes out. The Croupier lights the Drowned Oar again and plays knucklebones for timber or tallow, and the Loaded Bone is his. The Toothmonger opens her stall: she trades materials at fixed rates, and for 25 tallow, paid at once, she pawns a relic you name so that nothing on your next descent offers it; it holds your one town gift until you go down. The Peddler opens his barrow beside the Head-frame: three of his wares at a time, a blueprint for a set of the Lodge's furniture for curios or a rare dye for tallow, and a new three once a descent has ended; what you buy is yours for good. Three graves in the cemetery have been opened to the Drowned Mother, the Wrong Sun and the Many-Mouthed: raise one with iron, tallow and curios and its black candle is a town gift. Its patron's Attention starts at 1, so its first tier is on from floor 1 (and is the price), and it reaches out at the first break. Three tide-pools on the south shore hold a little timber, iron, tallow or a curio, and now and then a bottle; they fill again after each descent. Restore the Keeper's Lodge on the Rise, up either stair from the square, with timber and iron, and step inside: one room to lay a floor and a wall in and set furniture down, lifted, stored and salvaged as in the square, and a Grimoire on its podium, glowing for every creature met and relic found; tap it to read the book. The Grimoire floats over a podium and opens as you come near: lift it, turn it, set it down elsewhere or store it, but it can never be salvaged. Salvage on a lifted piece breaks it up at once. The two sconces on the back wall are yours to move or store as well, and furniture stands on a rug. A hatch in its floor opens on the Flooded Cellar, a ladder by its shelf climbs to the Attic: open each with the haul, and each is a room of its own to lay a floor and a wall in and furnish, its pieces turned, stored and salvaged as below. The Lodge’s pieces come in five sets, Fisherman’s and the Old Library from the start and the Drowned Chapel, the Brass Observatory and the Deep-One Coral by a blueprint from the Peddler's barrow; the set chip on the tray shows the next. Some hang on the back wall, and small things stand on a desk, a chest, a shelf or a table and go wherever it goes. Dye gives a lifted piece another colourway for tallow, and the Peddler's rare dyes join every piece they change. Its rooms are dark until you light them: tap a sconce, a lamp, a candle or a fireplace to light it or put it out, and every light throws the shadows of what stands near it. Each boss you put down on the stair leaves a trophy for the Lodge, one of each, carried up with the haul; tap it to read its Grimoire line. With the Lodge standing, two Keepers can work at chores at once. The Hearth Beacon stands cold below the Head-frame, at the head of the south lane: feed it tallow and curios, five times in all, and each time the rain thins and the dark lifts a little further round it, and more of what is carved in the stone under the square shows. It changes nothing on the stair. Mist lies along the shore and over the cemetery, thinner where the Hearth burns, and the plots lie darker than the square until something you build in them burns; neither changes anything you do, only what you see. A Keeper with no chore walks to a bench, to the Hearth once it burns, or into the Lodge to a stove, a fireplace or an armchair, and back; each has a favourite set, stays longer near it and says so, and the first time one of their favourites stands near their post they leave a note in chalk there, once: tap it to read. The cellar's brine rises a step each time a lamp goes out below and drains when you win the stair, and what it reached keeps its kelp and barnacles until the win after.
  • The stair. After each floor you take a gift, then choose one of three doors: a Merchant, a Shrine with pacts, something unknown, a quiet place to rest, a Reliquary with another gift, the Knucklebones (a game of bones against the hooded thing, for essence the stair would burn), or the Deep Stair straight down to an elite floor that pays a relic.
  • The toll. Your salvage from a floor is safe, but 70% of any other essence burns away when you take the stair. Spend it, or lose it. Bounties also thin out the deeper you go.
  • The shifting stair. The first three floors each have three maps and the last two have two; one is drawn as you reach the floor: where they climb out, how the road winds, where it forks, sometimes where the lamp stands. Its name sits beside the floor's. The waves are the same on every map. The stair's name decides which, and a saved floor keeps its own.
  • Every stair has a name. A descent is drawn from a seed: its maps, waves, Heralds, gifts, doors, omens, rooms and offers. The pause, death and morning screens name the stair and show its code; tap Copy to keep it. When the lamp goes out you can descend the same stair again, drawn the same way, though what the dark does in a fight is never the same twice. A stair walked twice leaves no embers.
  • Omens. Each door shows the omen waiting on the floor behind it: a smaller lamp, a swarm, faster creatures, kills that pay nothing. Choose your risks.
  • Trials. On the way to floors two and three, one door carries a Trial: the floor behind it plays by a rule, and passing it pays a relic. Rationed: six wards at most beside the path (what lies on the path, and horrors, don't count); the count sits beside the floor's name. The Hallowed Ground: beside the path you can build only on four patches marked in chalk, lit or dark; nothing there goes dark, a candle there burns without the lamp, a Tuning Fork there hums without the lamp's sound, and a pylon there powers the grid. Your wards there still strike only what is seen or heard. Sealed: two of your wards are locked for the floor, marked with a lock in the tray; never your light and never your harpoon. One of Each: each kind of ward stands only once, except what makes your light (candles of every kind, Tuning Forks, pylons, Bell Wires and Try-pots). Bare Hands: your rites are silent, all but the Bellringer's Toll. Unbranched: nothing can be upgraded, not even the lamp. The Long Night: candles shine half as far, Tuning Forks hum half as wide, and the lamp burns a tile smaller; it never comes with Moonless or Thick Dark.
  • Descents. On the landings after floors two, three and four, one door may carry a descent, marked with a cupped flame: the way down, played after the toll, before the next floor begins. Each pays and each costs. Failing one never ends the run, none leaves embers, and once walked it is not offered again that descent. The Carry: hold your thumb down anywhere to cup a small flame past a gallery of sleepers. A sleeper inside your light stirs; hidden, it settles. Hold too long and you stumble, spill the flask and flare. It pays the oil you carry down; every sleeper you wake adds dread on the next floor, and waking three loses the flask. The Mirror Stair: hold either side and drag up or down to swing that side's mirror, and hold its light on a cold sconce, following it up, until it catches. Each sconce lit widens the lamp below until its first wave breaks; each that rises out of reach unlit stays dark and narrows it. The Binding: the lantern sinks past a creature held in its light, named on the door. Before it, the stone asks a pledge from what the toll left: a share of your essence, or one of your relics, picked from three it draws (never a cursed one). Trace three sigils on a field of dots, dot to dot from the bright one; a wrong dot or a lift starts that sigil again. Draw all three in time and the creature is bound to you and the pledge comes back; fail and the stone keeps it. The Galvanist is never offered it. The Cast: iron rings hang on the walls, seen only in the lantern’s light, and the lantern swings as it sinks. Drag back and let go to cast a weighted line; it flies the other way, carried on by the swing, while the rings rise. Four lines, five rings. Each line costs a tenth of the essence you arrive with, never under 5 or over 20, caught or not. Each ring caught is a rite charge on the next floor, three at most, and a fourth gives back its line’s weight: tap a rite still cooling and it casts at once, its own wait running on as it was. The Smothering: four wicks burn in niches across a narrow tube, each a different brightness, and black fumes climb toward them. Tap them out dimmest first before the fumes reach them; a wick is snuffed when you lift, on the same wick. From the second plume they gutter and the order can change; two wicks almost alike both count as the dimmest. Three plumes. Each snuffed out clean, in order, makes the lamp hold one more oil for the rest of the run. Each wrong snuff, and each plume that smothers a wick still lit, is a dread on the next floor, three at most. The Occultist is never offered it. The Winch: drag left or right anywhere to steer the lantern down a shaft of black ribs, past arms that reach across it on a beat, fingers first. Your thumb’s sideways travel carries the lantern, a beat behind. Its cable hangs from a point over the middle, so let go and it swings back there; every jerk of the cable knocks it. A glint at the top marks where a purse will fall; be under it when it reaches the lantern. Each of the three is a tenth of the essence you arrive with, 4 to 12. Sometimes the last is a drowned man’s, pale, behind the tightest gap, and holds a relic, never a cursed one. Each rib or arm you snag on dims the lantern and costs the lamp 1 oil, 3 at most and never its last. Everything is paid when the shaft ends.
  • Relics. Relics bend the rules, and a cursed one takes as much as it gives. You are only offered a relic you can use: one that needs a ward, such as Salt or the Hex Effigy, waits until you can build it. Dead Reckoning, whose price falls on light, never comes to the Bellringer, who sees by sound. Tap a relic's seal to read it; a number on a seal is what it holds.
  • Patrons. Old things below the stair make offerings: the Drowned Mother, the Wrong Sun, and the Many-Mouthed. Half the time the landing's gift is one of theirs instead (a quarter, if one already reached out on that floor), and now and then one reaches out between waves; which one is a toss each time. Take one gift, or refuse. Every gift raises that patron's Attention, and Attention changes your floors. Her water speeds what walks in it, rises, and at last hides it. The Wrong Sun's bright spots show whatever stands in them, but a Stalker that crosses one has seen the lamp and runs; Watched, they sear, and the glare spreads to the stone beside them; Claimed, your wards in the glare fire slower. The Many-Mouthed reads what you built and sends its own up the stair as each wave begins, Gibberers for your wards and Gorgers for your horrors, and they leave nothing when they die; Watched, you carry dread and Gorgers snuff candles; Claimed, a Choir-Husk veils what walks near it, and bindings may break from Whispers. Their signs sit beside the Grimoire; tap one to see where you stand.
  • Conjunctions. Two patrons who have both noticed you, neither yet claiming you, may offer one gift together in place of the last of three. It is not shaped by your kit. The one whose Attention lags pays for it, and the other watches: the next wave, her water rises a tile, the Sun opens another spot, or one more Gibberer climbs. A descent takes one conjunction from each pair, and two at most. The Drowned Mother and the Wrong Sun: Phosphor Tide. The Drowned Mother and the Many-Mouthed: Gorger’s Undertow, Brine-Choir. The Wrong Sun and the Many-Mouthed: Sun-Drunk Chorus, Violet Husking.
  • Embers. Every descent, won or lost, leaves embers behind. Spend them in the Ember Hall on new kits, relics and stories. Carry the lamp to morning to open the Deeper Dark, where each depth adds a new cruelty.
  • The Grimoire. The book in the HUD holds every creature you have met, every ward and rite, and every relic you have found. The relics you carry sit beside it: tap one to read what it does.
  • Saving. The run saves at every break between waves. Save and quit from the pause menu, then Continue from the title.
  • The board turns. On a wide screen the map lies sideways so it can fill more of it. Rotate your device and it follows.
